scope: Woodford, Interest and Prices, Chapter 3: Optimizing Models with Nominal Rigidities, with Appendix B. Dixit-Stiglitz aggregation as genuine cost minimisation, real marginal cost and its elasticities as exact derivatives, flexible prices and the natural rate (Prop 3.1, corrected); prices fixed in advance and the New Classical Phillips curve (Prop 3.2); strategic complementarity, Kimball demand and intermediate inputs (Prop 3.3, Table 3.1); the Calvo index, the infinite-horizon reset problem and Prop 3.4; the New Keynesian Phillips curve from primitives (Prop 3.5); persistence and the contract multiplier (Props 3.6-3.7); the two-sector model (Prop 3.8); delays and indexation; sticky wages (Prop 3.9) and the joint wage-price dynamics.
source: Michael Woodford, Interest and Prices: Foundations of a Theory of Monetary Policy, Princeton University Press, 2003, Chapter 3, pp. 139-236, and Appendix B, pp. 656-669.
